SOURCE: "Recursive Multi-Agent Systems" (RecursiveMAS), Jiaru Zou (project lead), Rui Pan, Ruizhong Qiu, Pan Lu, Shizhe Diao, Jindong Jiang, Hanghang Tong, Tong Zhang, Markus J. Buehler, Jingrui He, James Zou. Stanford, UIUC, NVIDIA, MIT. arXiv:2604.25917v2 [cs.AI], 13 Jul 2026. Preprint, no venue stated. Project page recursivemas.github.io.

COVERAGE: All 96,367 chars read (body, references skimmed, appendices A-G). Appendix E (prompts) and F/G (case studies) read only at start and end; they are worked examples. Extraction is clean.

RELEVANCE VERDICT (plain): Weak and mostly off-topic for context engineering. It is a model-level method: agents pass last-layer hidden states ("latent thoughts") to each other through small trained adapters instead of text. It needs white-box access, frozen open-weight models, and training. It says nothing about context windows, context isolation, sub-agent summaries, or context rot. The only link to note 10 is that text hand-offs between agents cost tokens and latency, which the paper measures, but against a text baseline it built itself. Cite at most as a side reference ("agent-to-agent text is costly, and latent transfer is a research direction"). Do not use it as evidence for isolation or sub-agent design. Not a good fit to ground practical claims.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Latent-space hand-off cuts tokens and time versus text hand-off within the same recursive MAS structure.
  number: 34.6% / 65.5% / 75.6% fewer tokens and 1.2x / 1.9x / 2.4x speedup at recursion rounds r=1/2/3
  setup: sequential Planner-Critic-Solver; Light (sub-1.5B-class agents: Qwen3-1.7B, Llama3.2-1B, Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B) and Scaled (Gemma3-4B, Llama3.2-3B, Qwen3.5-4B); baseline is the authors' own Recursive-TextMAS; means over 5 runs; Table 2 averages across math, science and code benchmarks.
  quote: "RecursiveMASreduces the token usage by34.6%for the first recursion round, and the reduction scales to75.6%at 𝑟= 3."
  where: p.11 (Sec 5.4); Table 2 p.9
- Headline accuracy: +8.3% average over the strongest baseline on each benchmark.
  number: 8.3%
  setup: r=3, six benchmarks, frozen agents, only RecursiveLink trained; baselines given the same data and comparable training budget.
  quote: "achieving an average performance improvement of 8.3% over the strongest baseline on each benchmark"
  where: p.10 (Sec 5.2)
- Table 3 (r=3, Scaled): RecursiveMAS vs Recursive-TextMAS, in percent. MATH500 88.0 vs 85.8. AIME2025 86.7 vs 73.3. AIME2026 86.7 vs 73.3. GPQA-D 66.2 vs 61.6. LiveCodeBench 42.9 vs 38.7. MedQA 79.3 vs 77.0. Full-SFT single agent gets 83.2 / 73.3 / 76.7 / 62.8 / 38.6 / 77.0. Mixture-of-Agents is clearly weaker, with MATH500 79.8 and GPQA-D 47.6.
  quote: "RecursiveMAS88.0 86.7 86.7 66.2 42.9 79.3"
  where: p.10
- Text-based recursion does not improve with more rounds, and sometimes degrades. Recursive-TextMAS Light AIME2025 goes 24.0 (r=1), 23.3 (r=2), 18.0 (r=3). RecursiveMAS rises 30.7, 33.3, 34.0.
  quote: "Recursive-TextMAS ... Acc. 71.9 84.2 24.0 71.3" (r=1 row); r=3 row "69.1 85.8 18.0 73.3"
  where: p.9 Table 2
- Efficiency theory: replaces per-step vocabulary decoding cost m|V|d_h with m d_h^2 per agent.
  number: none (asymptotic)
  quote: "Since 𝑑ℎ≪|𝑉| in practice,RecursiveMASreplaces the expensive per-step vocabulary-space decoding cost𝑚|𝑉|𝑑ℎ with a much more efficient latent-space transformation𝑚𝑑2ℎ."
  where: p.6 (Remark 3.2); proof App A.1 p.21
- Gradient stability theorem: text-mediated links give gradient norm O(eps) (vanishing) when tokens are confident, while the residual RecursiveLink stays near 1. This is proved only under stated assumptions (Kaiming init, W3=I, norm bounds).
  quote: "directly applying text-based SFT (denoted byRtext(ℎ)) during recursion suffers from gradient vanishing"
  where: p.7; proof p.21-22
- Other collaboration patterns (Appendix D.1, Tables 6-8; only the ~6.2% / 4.8% / 8.0% figures come from the main text, p.11). Mixture: RecursiveMAS beats the best specialist by 6.2% on average. Deliberation (tool use): +4.8% over the Tool-Caller. Distillation: +8.0% over the Learner with 1.5x end-to-end speed advantage over the Expert, but still below the Expert (e.g. AIME2026 83.3 vs Expert 90.0).
  quote: "RecursiveMASimproves the learner by 8.0% while retaining 1.5× end-to-end speed advantage over the expert."
  where: p.11; Table 6 p.26
- Training is cheap because the LLMs are frozen. RecursiveMAS trains 13.12M parameters (0.31%), uses 15.29 GB peak GPU memory, costs $4.27 and reaches 74.9% average accuracy. LoRA gets 66.9% and Full-SFT 68.6%.
  quote: "RecursiveMAS15.29 13.12M (0.31%) $4.27 74.9"
  where: p.13 Table 5 (scaled sequential setting)
- Ablations. Latent thought length saturates around m=80 steps (Table 9: Math500 86.8 at 64-80, vs 83.3 at 0). RecursiveLink design: 2-layer residual is best (Table 4: GPQA-D 66.2 vs 63.2 for 1-layer). Training depth and inference depth are complementary (Fig 1).
  quote: "performance is stabilized across all benchmarks" (m≈80)
  where: p.12-13; Table 9 p.27

LIMITS
- The paper has no limitations section. The conclusion lists none. No failure analysis. Inferred, not conceded: the method is white-box (needs hidden states, trained adapters, open-weight models), so it cannot apply to API-only models such as Claude or GPT.
- The "text" comparator is the authors' own Recursive-TextMAS, which re-decodes full intermediate text each round. So the token and speed savings are measured against a deliberately naive text hand-off, not against summarised or isolated sub-agent context. Token counts for RecursiveMAS include only the final text and are "overall token usage"; the latent steps themselves are not counted as tokens.
- Gains versus the strongest baseline mix wide margins on AIME (30 problems each, Pass@10, so noisy) with small ones on MedQA/GPQA. Table 2 caption gives average std ±0.0041 accuracy over 5 runs, but no per-benchmark intervals.
- Models are small (1B-9B). Training data is s1K, m1k, OpenCodeReasoning and ARPO-SFT, with targets rewritten by Qwen3.5-397B-A17B. Search tasks (HotpotQA, Bamboogle) appear only in the Deliberation table and use an LLM judge (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B).
- Interpretability: latent messages cannot be read or audited by a human. The paper does not discuss this.

BUILDS ON
Looped/recursive LMs: LoopLM (Zhu et al., 2025); Geiping et al., 2025 (recurrent depth); Jolicoeur-Martineau, 2025 (tiny recursive networks); Bae et al., 2025 (Mixture-of-Recursions). Latent communication: Zou et al., 2025 ("Latent collaboration in multi-agent systems", same lead author); Du et al., 2025; Fu et al., 2025 (Cache-to-cache); Zheng et al., 2025; Ye et al., 2025a. MAS topologies and baselines: Mixture-of-Agents (Wang et al., 2025b); TextGrad (Yuksekgonul et al., 2025); MALT (Motwani et al., 2024); ChatDev (Qian et al., 2024); CAMEL (Li et al., 2023); Subramaniam et al., 2025. Training data: s1K (Muennighoff et al., 2025).

CODE: none. Equations worth keeping:
- Inner link (Eq 3, p.5): "Rin(ℎ)=ℎ+𝑊 2𝜎(𝑊1ℎ)"
- Outer link (Eq 4, p.5): "Rout(ℎ)=𝑊 3ℎ+𝑊 2𝜎(𝑊1ℎ)"
- Prompt template with the latent placeholder (App E, p.28): "You are a planner agent in a recursive multi-agent system. Here is the latent information from previous round: {Latent Thought Embeddings}."

FIGURES
- Fig 2 (p.4): architecture. Agents A1..AN form a loop, with inner links per agent and outer links between agents. Only the last agent decodes text, and only in the final round. Shows the idea fastest.
- Fig 4 (p.6): two-stage training, inner-loop warm start then outer-loop backprop through all rounds.
- Fig 5 and 6 (p.11): speedup and token-reduction bars by round. These are the only figures relevant to the note's cost-of-text-handoff point.
- Fig 1 (p.1): scaling landscape over training and inference depth.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Equations are partly garbled in the extraction (spacing, matrix norms), but all quoted numbers are intact. Table 2 columns are flattened, so per-cell attribution (Light vs Scaled) comes from the order of values, not from labels. The abstract's "1.2x-2.4x" and "34.6%-75.6%" are the r=1 to r=3 range, not a range across methods. Table 2 says r=2 token reduction is 65.5%.
